fuentes/incompletitud-godel/titulo.texto: On Formally Undecidable Propositions of Principia Mathematica and Related Systems

fuentes/incompletitud-godel/soporte.texto: Monatshefte für Mathematik und Physik, vol. 38

fuentes/incompletitud-godel/resumen.texto: Gödel proves that every consistent formal system capable of expressing arithmetic contains true statements that it cannot prove, and that it cannot prove its own consistency either. To do so he encodes formulas and proofs as numbers.

fuentes/incompletitud-godel/por_que_impo.texto: It set a limit on Hilbert's program to provide a foundation for all of mathematics and was the starting point for the work of Church and Turing on computability.

fuentes/sobre-los-numeros-computables/ti.texto: On Computable Numbers, with an Application to the Entscheidungsproblem

fuentes/sobre-los-numeros-computables/so.texto: Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society, series 2, vol. 42

fuentes/sobre-los-numeros-computables/re.texto: Turing defines an abstract machine that reads and writes symbols on a tape according to a table of rules, and a universal machine able to imitate any other when given its description. With it he proves that there is no general procedure for deciding whether a logical statement is provable, the decision problem posed by Hilbert. Alonzo Church had reached the same result by another route shortly before.

fuentes/sobre-los-numeros-computables/po.texto: It established the definition of computability and anticipated the stored-program computer: it is the founding text of computer science.

fuentes/sobre-los-numeros-computables/le.texto: Text of the article in PDF (University of Virginia)

fuentes/teoria-de-juegos/titulo.texto: Theory of Games and Economic Behavior

fuentes/teoria-de-juegos/soporte.texto: Book (Princeton University Press), with Oskar Morgenstern

fuentes/teoria-de-juegos/resumen.texto: Von Neumann and the economist Oskar Morgenstern formalize situations in which several agents with opposing interests make decisions that affect one another. They develop the minimax theorem for zero-sum games and an axiomatic theory of expected utility.

fuentes/teoria-de-juegos/por_que_importa.texto: It founded game theory, later used in economics, Cold War nuclear strategy, evolutionary biology and computer science.

fuentes/mcculloch-pitts/titulo.texto: A Logical Calculus of the Ideas Immanent in Nervous Activity

fuentes/mcculloch-pitts/resumen.texto: The neurophysiologist Warren McCulloch and the logician Walter Pitts model the neuron as a unit that fires or not depending on the sum of its inputs, and show that networks of such neurons can compute any function of propositional logic.

fuentes/mcculloch-pitts/por_que_importa.texto: It is the first mathematical model of a neural network, a forerunner of the perceptron and of deep learning.

fuentes/tesis-de-shannon/titulo.texto: A Symbolic Analysis of Relay and Switching Circuits

fuentes/tesis-de-shannon/soporte.texto: Master's thesis (MIT; written in 1937, degree awarded in 1940); published in Transactions of the American Institute of Electrical Engineers, vol. 57 (1938)

fuentes/tesis-de-shannon/resumen.texto: Shannon shows that Boolean algebra describes the behaviour of circuits of relays and switches, so that a circuit can be designed and simplified through logical calculation; and, conversely, that relays can carry out logical and arithmetic operations.

fuentes/tesis-de-shannon/por_que_importa.texto: It is the theoretical basis of digital circuit design.

fuentes/primer-borrador-edvac/titulo.texto: First Draft of a Report on the EDVAC

fuentes/primer-borrador-edvac/soporte.texto: Mimeographed report of the Moore School of the University of Pennsylvania (30 June 1945), under contract with the U.S. Army

fuentes/primer-borrador-edvac/resumen.texto: Von Neumann describes the logic of the computer that would succeed the ENIAC: an arithmetic unit, a control unit, a memory that stores both data and instructions, and input and output devices, all using binary numbers. The text summarized discussions with J. Presper Eckert, John Mauchly and other members of the team, but it circulated under his name alone.

fuentes/primer-borrador-edvac/por_que_im.texto: It spread the stored-program architecture, known ever since as the “von Neumann architecture”, which almost all computers follow.

fuentes/primer-borrador-edvac/leer.0.tit.texto: First draft of a report on the EDVAC (MIT copy)

fuentes/as-we-may-think/resumen.texto: With the war over, Bush proposes that scientists devote themselves to making accumulated knowledge accessible. He describes the “memex”, a microfilm desk in which each person stores their books and documents and links them with associative “trails” that can be shared with others.

fuentes/as-we-may-think/por_que_importa.texto: It anticipated hypertext and the personal computer; it inspired Douglas Engelbart and the creators of the web.

fuentes/cibernetica-wiener/titulo.texto: Cybernetics: Or Control and Communication in the Animal and the Machine

fuentes/cibernetica-wiener/resumen.texto: Wiener, an MIT mathematician, combines his wartime work on anti-aircraft fire control with neurophysiology and proposes a common science of systems that regulate themselves through feedback, whether organisms or machines. He devotes chapters to computers and warns about the effects of automation on work.

fuentes/cibernetica-wiener/por_que_impor.texto: It gave its name to cybernetics, which influenced control theory, artificial intelligence and the social sciences.

fuentes/teoria-matematica-de-la-comunica.texto: Bell System Technical Journal, vol. 27 (July and October 1948)

Shannon defines information as a reduction of uncertainty and measures it in bits (a word he attributes to John Tukey) by means of entropy. He proves that every noisy channel has a maximum capacity and that, below it, there exist codes that allow transmission with as few errors as desired.
It founded information theory, the basis of data compression, error correction and digital telecommunications.
Part one, in the Bell System Technical Journal archive (Internet Archive)

fuentes/maquinaria-computacional-e-intel.texto: Turing replaces the question “Can machines think?” with an “imitation game”: whether an interrogator, communicating in writing, fails to tell a machine from a person. He answers nine objections (the theological, the mathematical, the argument from consciousness and Lady Lovelace's, among others) and proposes building machines that learn like a child.
It set out the Turing test and the program of artificial intelligence six years before the field had a name.
Text of the 1950 Mind article in PDF (University of Maryland, Baltimore County)

fuentes/el-transistor/soporte.texto: Physical Review, vol. 74 (letter by John Bardeen and Walter Brattain, July 1948)

fuentes/el-transistor/resumen.texto: Bardeen and Brattain describe a germanium device with two closely spaced point contacts in which a small current controls a larger one, so that it amplifies signals like a vacuum tube. Bell Laboratories had presented it to the press in June 1948.

fuentes/el-transistor/por_que_importa.texto: It launched solid-state electronics; William Shockley, Bardeen and Brattain received the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics.

fuentes/propuesta-de-dartmouth/titulo.texto: A Proposal for the Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence

fuentes/propuesta-de-dartmouth/soporte.texto: Proposal to the Rockefeller Foundation (August 31, 1955), signed by John McCarthy, Marvin Minsky, Nathaniel Rochester and Claude Shannon

fuentes/propuesta-de-dartmouth/resumen.texto: The signatories request funding for ten researchers to spend two months at Dartmouth College studying “the conjecture that every aspect of learning or any other feature of intelligence can in principle be so precisely described that a machine can be made to simulate it”. They list topics: language, neural networks, abstraction, self-improvement and creativity.

fuentes/propuesta-de-dartmouth/por_que_i.texto: It coined the term “artificial intelligence” and convened the 1956 workshop regarded as the founding of the field.

fuentes/propuesta-de-dartmouth/leer.0.ti.texto: Text on John McCarthy's Stanford website

fuentes/perceptron-de-rosenblatt/titulo.texto: The Perceptron: A Probabilistic Model for Information Storage and Organization in the Brain

fuentes/perceptron-de-rosenblatt/resumen.texto: Rosenblatt describes a network of connected units whose weights are adjusted with experience, so that it learns to recognize patterns without being programmed with rules. The model was built as the Mark I Perceptron, an image-classification machine funded by the US Navy.

fuentes/perceptron-de-rosenblatt/por_que.texto: It was the first machine learning system based on neural networks; its learning rule lies at the foundation of deep learning.

fuentes/lisp-mccarthy/titulo.texto: Recursive Functions of Symbolic Expressions and Their Computation by Machine

fuentes/lisp-mccarthy/soporte.texto: Communications of the ACM, vol. 3, no. 4 (April 1960)

fuentes/lisp-mccarthy/resumen.texto: McCarthy presents Lisp, a language in which programs and data are lists, with recursive functions, conditional expressions and automatic reclamation of unused memory. He shows that a universal function written in the same language can interpret any Lisp program.

fuentes/lisp-mccarthy/por_que_importa.texto: Lisp was the main language of artificial intelligence for decades and introduced ideas that most modern languages adopted.

fuentes/lisp-mccarthy/leer.0.titulo.texto: Text on John McCarthy's Stanford website

fuentes/simbiosis-hombre-computadora/sop.texto: IRE Transactions on Human Factors in Electronics, vol. HFE-1 (March 1960)

fuentes/simbiosis-hombre-computadora/res.texto: Licklider proposes that people and computers cooperate in real time: the machine would do the routine work of calculation and search, and the person would set the goals and evaluate the results. He lists what is still needed to achieve this: time-sharing, large memories, languages close to natural language and screens for drawing.

fuentes/simbiosis-hombre-computadora/por.texto: It set the agenda for interactive computing, which Licklider later funded from ARPA.

fuentes/simbiosis-hombre-computadora/lee.texto: Text of the article (MIT, Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory)

fuentes/aumentar-el-intelecto-humano/tit.texto: Augmenting Human Intellect: A Conceptual Framework

fuentes/aumentar-el-intelecto-humano/sop.texto: Report to the US Air Force Office of Scientific Research (Stanford Research Institute, October 1962)

fuentes/aumentar-el-intelecto-humano/res.texto: Engelbart proposes using computers to augment people's ability to solve complex problems, combining artifacts, language, methodology and training. He imagines a professional who writes, links and rearranges texts and symbols on a screen.

fuentes/aumentar-el-intelecto-humano/por.texto: It is the program of the laboratory that invented the mouse and demonstrated hypertext in 1968.

fuentes/patente-de-kilby/titulo.texto: Miniaturized Electronic Circuits (Kilby's integrated circuit patent)

fuentes/patente-de-kilby/soporte.texto: US Patent 3,138,743 (filed 1959, granted 1964), assigned to Texas Instruments

fuentes/patente-de-kilby/resumen.texto: Kilby describes a circuit in which resistors, capacitors and transistors are formed in a single body of semiconductor material instead of being made separately and soldered together. The 1958 prototype was made of germanium and its components were joined with gold wires.

fuentes/patente-de-kilby/por_que_importa.texto: It is the first integrated circuit patent; Kilby received the 2000 Nobel Prize in Physics for it.

fuentes/patente-de-kilby/leer.0.titulo.texto: Patent text and images on Google Patents

fuentes/patente-de-noyce/titulo.texto: Semiconductor Device-and-Lead Structure (Noyce's integrated circuit patent)

fuentes/patente-de-noyce/soporte.texto: US Patent 2,981,877 (filed 1959, granted 1961), assigned to Fairchild Semiconductor

fuentes/patente-de-noyce/resumen.texto: Noyce proposes making the components in a silicon wafer using Jean Hoerni's planar process and connecting them with metal strips deposited on an insulating oxide layer, without loose wires. Texas Instruments and Fairchild disputed priority for the invention and eventually agreed to cross-license.

fuentes/patente-de-noyce/por_que_importa.texto: His monolithic silicon design is the one that went into mass production and led to microchips.

fuentes/patente-de-noyce/leer.0.titulo.texto: Patent text and images on Google Patents

fuentes/ley-de-moore/titulo.texto: Cramming More Components onto Integrated Circuits

fuentes/ley-de-moore/resumen.texto: Moore, director of research at Fairchild, observes that the number of components per integrated circuit at minimum cost had doubled every year and predicts that this will continue for at least ten years, reaching about 65,000 components by 1975. He anticipates home computers, electronic controls for cars and personal communication equipment.

fuentes/ley-de-moore/por_que_importa.texto: His prediction, revised in 1975 to a doubling every two years, served as a target for the semiconductor industry for half a century.

fuentes/computadora-como-dispositivo-de-.texto: The Computer as a Communication Device
Science and Technology (April 1968), with Robert Taylor

Licklider and Robert Taylor, then director of ARPA's computing office, argue that networked computers will above all be a medium for people to communicate and work together. They envision online communities united by common interests rather than by geography.
It anticipated the social use of networks shortly before ARPANET began operating.

fuentes/perceptrons-libro/resumen.texto: Minsky and Papert analyze mathematically what single-layer perceptrons can and cannot recognize: they show, for example, that they cannot determine whether a figure is connected or compute the “exclusive or” function. They leave open, skeptically, the question of multilayer networks.

fuentes/perceptrons-libro/por_que_import.texto: It contributed to the abandonment of neural network research during the 1970s, until backpropagation spread in the 1980s.

fuentes/dynabook/titulo.texto: A Personal Computer for Children of All Ages

fuentes/dynabook/soporte.texto: Proceedings of the ACM National Conference (Boston, August 1972)

fuentes/dynabook/resumen.texto: Kay describes the Dynabook, a notebook-sized computer with a flat screen, keyboard and network connection, designed for children to learn by programming, reading and drawing. He estimates that it could come to cost the same as a television set.

fuentes/dynabook/por_que_importa.texto: It envisioned the laptop and the tablet, and guided PARC's work on graphical interfaces and the Smalltalk language.

fuentes/sistema-unix/soporte.texto: Communications of the ACM, vol. 17, no. 7 (July 1974), with Ken Thompson

fuentes/sistema-unix/resumen.texto: Ritchie and Thompson describe the operating system they had been writing since 1969 for PDP minicomputers: a hierarchical file system, devices treated as files, a replaceable command interpreter and processes chained together with “pipes”. The system was written almost entirely in C.

fuentes/sistema-unix/por_que_importa.texto: Unix and its descendants and derivatives (BSD, Linux, macOS, Android) became the foundation of servers, phones and the internet.

fuentes/ethernet/titulo.texto: Ethernet: Distributed Packet Switching for Local Computer Networks

fuentes/ethernet/soporte.texto: Communications of the ACM, vol. 19, no. 7 (July 1976), with David Boggs

fuentes/ethernet/resumen.texto: Metcalfe and Boggs describe the local network that had been running at Xerox PARC since 1973: the computers share a coaxial cable, each one listens before transmitting and, if two packets collide, they wait a random time and try again.

fuentes/ethernet/por_que_importa.texto: Ethernet, standardized in 1983 as IEEE 802.3, remains the most widely used technology in wired local networks.

fuentes/ethernet/leer.0.titulo.texto: Xerox PARC technical report CSL-75-7 (1975), preprint version of the article (Bitsavers)

fuentes/el-lenguaje-de-programacion-c/re.texto: Kernighan and Ritchie present the C language, created by Ritchie c. 1972 to rewrite Unix, with examples that begin with the “hello, world” program. The book served as the language's specification until the 1989 ANSI standard.

fuentes/el-lenguaje-de-programacion-c/po.texto: C became the language of operating systems and system software, and its syntax passed into C++, Java, JavaScript and many other languages.

fuentes/hopfield-1982/titulo.texto: Neural Networks and Physical Systems with Emergent Collective Computational Abilities

fuentes/hopfield-1982/soporte.texto: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, vol. 79 (April 1982)

fuentes/hopfield-1982/resumen.texto: Hopfield describes a network of interconnected binary neurons whose dynamics reduce an “energy”, as in a magnetic system. Memories are stored as minima of that energy, and the network retrieves them from an incomplete or noisy version.

fuentes/hopfield-1982/por_que_importa.texto: It brought statistical physics to the study of neural networks and revived the field; it was one of the works recognized with the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics.

fuentes/retropropagacion/soporte.texto: Nature, vol. 323 (October 9, 1986), with Geoffrey Hinton and Ronald Williams

fuentes/retropropagacion/resumen.texto: The authors show that a multilayer neural network can be trained by calculating how much each connection contributes to the output error and adjusting the weights backward, layer by layer. In this way, the hidden layers learn useful internal representations that no one programmed. The method had precedents, such as Paul Werbos's thesis (1974).

fuentes/retropropagacion/por_que_importa.texto: It popularized the algorithm used to train virtually all of today's neural networks.

fuentes/anatomia-de-google/titulo.texto: The Anatomy of a Large-Scale Hypertextual Web Search Engine

fuentes/anatomia-de-google/soporte.texto: Computer Networks and ISDN Systems, vol. 30 (proceedings of the 7th International World Wide Web Conference, Brisbane), with Larry Page

fuentes/anatomia-de-google/resumen.texto: Brin and Page describe the Google prototype, which indexed some 24 million pages. They propose ranking results with PageRank, which measures a page's importance by how many important pages link to it, and using the text of links to describe the target page.

fuentes/anatomia-de-google/por_que_impor.texto: PageRank was the basis of the world's most widely used search engine and of the company Google, founded that same year.

fuentes/alexnet/titulo.texto: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks

fuentes/alexnet/soporte.texto: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 25 (NeurIPS 2012), with Ilya Sutskever and Geoffrey Hinton

fuentes/alexnet/resumen.texto: The authors use two graphics processors to train an eight-layer convolutional network with 60 million parameters on 1.2 million ImageNet images. In the 2012 competition its error rate was 15.3%, against 26.2% for the second-best system.

fuentes/alexnet/por_que_importa.texto: It triggered the deep learning boom and the use of graphics processors to train neural networks.

fuentes/alphago-nature/titulo.texto: Mastering the Game of Go with Deep Neural Networks and Tree Search

fuentes/alphago-nature/autor.texto: David Silver, Aja Huang, Demis Hassabis and others (DeepMind)

fuentes/alphago-nature/resumen.texto: The DeepMind team describes AlphaGo, which combines neural networks trained on expert games and on self-play with Monte Carlo tree search. It reports that the program beat European champion Fan Hui 5–0 in October 2015, the first defeat of a professional go player by a computer without a handicap.

fuentes/alphago-nature/por_que_importa.texto: It announced a milestone expected to be a decade away; two months later AlphaGo defeated Lee Sedol.

fuentes/attention-is-all-you-need/soport.texto: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30 (NeurIPS 2017); preprint on arXiv (1706.03762)

fuentes/attention-is-all-you-need/resume.texto: Eight Google researchers propose the transformer, a machine translation architecture that dispenses with recurrent networks and relies solely on attention mechanisms, which weigh the relationships among all the words in a sequence at once. It achieves better results in English-to-German and English-to-French translation with less training time, because the computation can be parallelized.

fuentes/attention-is-all-you-need/por_qu.texto: The transformer is the basis of large language models, such as GPT, and of many imaging and biology systems.

fuentes/gpt-3/soporte.texto: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33 (NeurIPS 2020); preprint on arXiv (2005.14165)

fuentes/gpt-3/resumen.texto: OpenAI presents GPT-3, a 175-billion-parameter transformer trained on internet text and books. It shows that, without retraining, the model solves new tasks (translating, answering questions, doing simple arithmetic) from a few instructions or examples written in the text, and discusses its biases and potential misuse.

fuentes/gpt-3/por_que_importa.texto: It showed that scaling up language models gives them general capabilities; a derived model, GPT-3.5, was the basis of ChatGPT (2022).

fuentes/alphafold/titulo.texto: Highly Accurate Protein Structure Prediction with AlphaFold

fuentes/alphafold/soporte.texto: Nature, vol. 596 (August 2021), with Demis Hassabis and others

fuentes/alphafold/resumen.texto: The DeepMind team describes AlphaFold 2, a neural network that predicts the three-dimensional shape of a protein from its amino acid sequence. In the CASP14 assessment (2020) it achieved, in most cases, an accuracy comparable to that of experimental methods.

fuentes/alphafold/por_que_importa.texto: It largely solved a problem that had been open for fifty years; Hassabis and Jumper shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with David Baker.

fuentes/baran-comunicaciones-distribuida.texto: Series of eleven RAND Corporation memoranda (RM-3420 and following, August 1964)

Baran proposes a network without a center, with many redundant paths between the nodes, in which messages are divided into “blocks” that travel separately and are reassembled at the destination. His goal was for US military communications to survive a nuclear attack.
It is one of the two independent origins of packet switching, the basis of the internet.

fuentes/davies-propuesta-npl/titulo.texto: Proposal for a Digital Communication Network

fuentes/davies-propuesta-npl/soporte.texto: Internal report of the UK National Physical Laboratory (June 1966)

fuentes/davies-propuesta-npl/resumen.texto: Davies proposes a national network that would transmit data between computers divided into short “packets”, so as to use the lines better than dedicated circuits would. A reduced version was built as the laboratory’s local network, which operated in part from 1969 and fully from January 1970.

fuentes/davies-propuesta-npl/por_que_imp.texto: It coined the term “packet”; his work influenced the design of ARPANET.

fuentes/rfc-1/soporte.texto: Request for Comments no. 1 (April 7, 1969), Network Working Group

fuentes/rfc-1/resumen.texto: Crocker, a UCLA student, summarizes the ideas of the group designing how the host computers (“hosts”) connected to the IMPs, ARPANET's switching nodes, would communicate. He presents it as provisional notes open to discussion.

fuentes/rfc-1/por_que_importa.texto: It launched the RFC series, the open format in which internet protocols are still defined.

fuentes/rfc-1/leer.0.titulo.texto: Text on the RFC Editor website

fuentes/protocolo-tcp/titulo.texto: A Protocol for Packet Network Intercommunication

fuentes/protocolo-tcp/soporte.texto: IEEE Transactions on Communications, vol. 22, no. 5 (May 1974), with Robert Kahn

fuentes/protocolo-tcp/resumen.texto: Cerf and Kahn propose interconnecting different packet networks (cable, radio or satellite) through gateways and a transmission control program on each computer, which numbers the data, reorders it, retransmits what is lost and regulates the flow. The differences between the networks remain hidden from users.

fuentes/protocolo-tcp/por_que_importa.texto: It is the original design of TCP/IP, the internet protocol suite; Cerf and Kahn received the 2004 Turing Award.

fuentes/rfc-791/soporte.texto: Request for Comments no. 791 (September 1981), prepared for DARPA

fuentes/rfc-791/resumen.texto: It specifies version 4 of the IP protocol: the datagram format, 32-bit addresses and the fragmentation of packets as they pass between networks. It was published together with RFC 793, which specifies TCP.

fuentes/rfc-791/por_que_importa.texto: IPv4 still carries much of the internet's traffic; ARPANET adopted TCP/IP on January 1, 1983.

fuentes/rfc-791/leer.0.titulo.texto: Text on the RFC Editor website

fuentes/rfc-dns/resumen.texto: Mockapetris replaces the single table of computer names distributed by the Stanford Research Institute with a hierarchical, distributed database in which each domain delegates to servers responsible for its subdomains.

fuentes/rfc-dns/por_que_importa.texto: The Domain Name System (DNS) makes it possible to use names instead of numeric addresses across the internet; RFCs 1034 and 1035 (1987) updated it.

fuentes/rfc-dns/leer.0.titulo.texto: RFC 882 on the RFC Editor website

fuentes/rfc-dns/leer.1.titulo.texto: RFC 883 on the RFC Editor website

fuentes/propuesta-de-la-web/resumen.texto: Berners-Lee proposes solving the loss of information at CERN with a distributed hypertext system: documents stored on different computers, joined by links and accessible from any terminal. His supervisor, Mike Sendall, wrote “vague but exciting” on the cover.

fuentes/propuesta-de-la-web/por_que_impo.texto: It is the origin of the World Wide Web; CERN released the web software for public use in 1993.

fuentes/propuesta-de-la-web/leer.1.titul.texto: Original on the CERN Document Server

fuentes/ley-de-planck/titulo.texto: On the Law of Distribution of Energy in the Normal Spectrum

fuentes/ley-de-planck/soporte.texto: Verhandlungen der Deutschen Physikalischen Gesellschaft (communication of December 14, 1900); Annalen der Physik, vol. 4 (1901)

fuentes/ley-de-planck/resumen.texto: To derive the formula describing black-body radiation, Planck assumes that the oscillators in the walls exchange energy only in discrete amounts, proportional to the frequency (E = hν). He thus introduces the constant h, which now bears his name.

fuentes/ley-de-planck/por_que_importa.texto: It marks the birth of quantum physics; Planck received the 1918 Nobel Prize in Physics.

fuentes/tesis-de-marie-curie/soporte.texto: Doctoral thesis (Faculty of Sciences of Paris, 1903), published by Gauthier-Villars

fuentes/tesis-de-marie-curie/resumen.texto: Curie brings together her research since 1897: radioactivity as a property of the atoms of certain elements, the discovery of polonium and radium with Pierre Curie (1898) and the determination of the atomic weight of radium.

fuentes/tesis-de-marie-curie/por_que_imp.texto: It founded the study of radioactivity; that same year she received the Nobel Prize in Physics with Pierre Curie and Henri Becquerel, and in 1911 the Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

fuentes/tesis-de-marie-curie/leer.0.titu.texto: French text of the first edition (1903), Wikisource

fuentes/annus-mirabilis/resumen.texto: While working at the patent office in Bern, Einstein published four papers in 1905: one on light quanta and the photoelectric effect, another on Brownian motion as evidence for the existence of atoms, the one on special relativity and the one that derives the equivalence of mass and energy. That same year he submitted his doctoral thesis on the size of molecules.

fuentes/annus-mirabilis/por_que_importa.texto: They changed 20th-century physics: they opened up the quantum physics of light, confirmed atomic theory and redefined space and time.

fuentes/annus-mirabilis/leer.0.titulo.texto: Article on the photoelectric effect, Annalen der Physik 1905 (PDF, University of Augsburg)

fuentes/annus-mirabilis/leer.1.titulo.texto: Article on Brownian motion, Annalen der Physik 1905 (PDF, University of Augsburg)

fuentes/efecto-fotoelectrico-einstein/ti.texto: On a Heuristic Point of View Concerning the Production and Transformation of Light

fuentes/efecto-fotoelectrico-einstein/re.texto: Einstein proposes that light behaves as if it were made up of independent quanta of energy, and with this hypothesis he explains the photoelectric effect: the energy of the electrons that light knocks out of a metal depends on its frequency, not its intensity.

fuentes/efecto-fotoelectrico-einstein/po.texto: It introduced the light quantum, later called the photon; Einstein received the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics for the law of the photoelectric effect. It is the basis of solar cells and image sensors.

fuentes/efecto-fotoelectrico-einstein/le.texto: German text, Annalen der Physik 17 (1905), PDF from the University of Augsburg

fuentes/movimiento-browniano-einstein/ti.texto: On the Motion of Small Particles Suspended in Liquids at Rest Required by the Molecular-Kinetic Theory of Heat

fuentes/movimiento-browniano-einstein/re.texto: Einstein calculates that, if heat is the motion of molecules, microscopic particles suspended in a liquid must move randomly with a measurable mean displacement. Jean Perrin confirmed the prediction experimentally in 1908.

fuentes/movimiento-browniano-einstein/po.texto: It was the decisive proof of the existence of atoms and molecules, still disputed in 1905.

fuentes/movimiento-browniano-einstein/le.texto: German text, Annalen der Physik 17 (1905), PDF from the University of Augsburg

fuentes/electrodinamica-de-los-cuerpos-e.texto: On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies

From two postulates, that the laws of physics are the same for all observers in uniform motion and that the speed of light in a vacuum is constant, Einstein deduces that time and lengths depend on the observer and that there is no absolute simultaneity. In this way he reconciles mechanics with Maxwell's electromagnetism without the need for the ether.
It is the special theory of relativity, the basis of particle physics and necessary, together with general relativity, for GPS to work.

fuentes/inercia-y-energia/titulo.texto: Does the Inertia of a Body Depend Upon Its Energy Content?

fuentes/inercia-y-energia/resumen.texto: In three pages, Einstein deduces from special relativity that a body emitting an energy E loses a mass E/c², and concludes that mass is a measure of energy content. He suggests testing it with radium salts.

fuentes/inercia-y-energia/por_que_import.texto: It formulated the equivalence of mass and energy (E = mc²), which explains the energy released in nuclear reactions.

fuentes/modelo-de-rutherford/titulo.texto: The Scattering of α and β Particles by Matter and the Structure of the Atom

fuentes/modelo-de-rutherford/resumen.texto: To explain why some alpha particles fired at a gold foil bounced back at large angles, as Hans Geiger and Ernest Marsden had observed, Rutherford proposes that almost all the mass and positive charge of the atom are concentrated in a tiny nucleus.

fuentes/modelo-de-rutherford/por_que_imp.texto: It introduced the atomic nucleus and opened up nuclear physics.

fuentes/modelo-de-rutherford/leer.0.titu.texto: Philosophical Magazine 21 (1911), PDF scan (University of Tübingen)

fuentes/modelo-de-bohr/titulo.texto: On the Constitution of Atoms and Molecules

fuentes/modelo-de-bohr/resumen.texto: Bohr applies Planck's quantization to Rutherford's atom: the electron can only occupy certain stable orbits and emits or absorbs light when it jumps between them. With this model he calculates the lines of the hydrogen spectrum.

fuentes/modelo-de-bohr/por_que_importa.texto: It was the first quantum model of the atom; Bohr received the 1922 Nobel Prize in Physics.

fuentes/relatividad-general/soporte.texto: Sitzungsberichte der Preußischen Akademie der Wissenschaften (25 November 1915); full exposition in Annalen der Physik, vol. 49 (1916)

fuentes/relatividad-general/resumen.texto: Einstein presents the equations that relate the curvature of spacetime to the matter and energy it contains: gravity ceases to be a force and becomes geometry. A week earlier he had shown that the theory explains the advance of Mercury's perihelion and predicts that starlight is deflected when passing close to the Sun.

fuentes/relatividad-general/por_que_impo.texto: It is the general theory of relativity, the basis of modern cosmology and of the study of black holes and gravitational waves.

fuentes/relatividad-general/leer.0.titul.texto: English translation of the 1916 article on Wikisource

fuentes/eclipse-de-1919-informe/titulo.texto: A Determination of the Deflection of Light by the Sun's Gravitational Field

fuentes/eclipse-de-1919-informe/autor.texto: Frank Dyson, Arthur Eddington and Charles Davidson

fuentes/eclipse-de-1919-informe/soporte.texto: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A, vol. 220

fuentes/eclipse-de-1919-informe/resumen.texto: It reports the results of the British expeditions to Sobral (Brazil) and the island of Príncipe, which photographed the stars near the Sun during the total eclipse of 1919. The measured deflections were close to the 1.75 arcseconds predicted by Einstein and not to half that value, which Newtonian gravitation gave. The selection of the data was later disputed, but subsequent measurements confirmed the result.

fuentes/eclipse-de-1919-informe/por_que_.texto: Its announcement, in November 1919, made Einstein a world figure.

fuentes/mecanica-matricial/titulo.texto: Quantum-Theoretical Re-interpretation of Kinematic and Mechanical Relations

fuentes/mecanica-matricial/resumen.texto: Heisenberg proposes building the theory of the atom solely from observable quantities, such as the frequencies and intensities of the light emitted, and not from orbits that cannot be observed. Max Born and Pascual Jordan recognized matrix algebra in his tables of numbers and used it to develop matrix mechanics.

fuentes/mecanica-matricial/por_que_impor.texto: It marks the beginning of quantum mechanics; Heisenberg received the 1932 Nobel Prize in Physics.

fuentes/ecuacion-de-schrodinger/soporte.texto: Annalen der Physik, vols. 79 to 81 (series of four articles)

fuentes/ecuacion-de-schrodinger/resumen.texto: Schrödinger describes the electron with a wave function that obeys a differential equation; the energy levels of the hydrogen atom appear as the allowed solutions of that equation. Shortly afterwards he showed that his wave mechanics is equivalent to Heisenberg's matrix mechanics.

fuentes/ecuacion-de-schrodinger/por_que_.texto: The Schrödinger equation is the basic tool of quantum chemistry and materials physics; 1933 Nobel Prize in Physics.

fuentes/principio-de-incertidumbre/titul.texto: On the Intuitive Content of Quantum Kinematics and Mechanics

fuentes/principio-de-incertidumbre/resum.texto: Heisenberg shows that the position and momentum of a particle cannot both be known with arbitrary precision at the same time: the product of their uncertainties has a minimum of the order of Planck's constant. He illustrates this with an imaginary gamma-ray microscope.

fuentes/principio-de-incertidumbre/por_q.texto: The uncertainty principle is central to the interpretation of quantum mechanics.

fuentes/ley-de-hubble/titulo.texto: A Relation between Distance and Radial Velocity among Extra-Galactic Nebulae

fuentes/ley-de-hubble/soporte.texto: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, vol. 15

fuentes/ley-de-hubble/resumen.texto: Using distances estimated from variable stars and velocities measured by Vesto Slipher and Milton Humason, Hubble shows that galaxies recede faster the farther away they are. Georges Lemaître had published a similar relation in 1927, as a consequence of an expanding universe.

fuentes/ley-de-hubble/por_que_importa.texto: It was the observational proof of the expansion of the universe, the basis of the Big Bang theory; since 2018 the International Astronomical Union has recommended calling it the Hubble–Lemaître law.

fuentes/ley-de-hubble/leer.0.titulo.texto: Text of the article in PNAS 15 (1929), PubMed Central

fuentes/existencia-del-neutron/resumen.texto: Chadwick explains the penetrating radiation emitted by beryllium bombarded with alpha particles as a stream of uncharged particles with a mass similar to that of the proton: the neutron, whose existence Rutherford had anticipated.

fuentes/existencia-del-neutron/por_que_i.texto: Having no charge, the neutron penetrates nuclei: it was the tool that led to nuclear fission. Chadwick received the 1935 Nobel Prize in Physics.

fuentes/hahn-strassmann-1939/titulo.texto: On the Detection and Characteristics of the Alkaline Earth Metals Formed by Irradiation of Uranium with Neutrons

fuentes/hahn-strassmann-1939/soporte.texto: Die Naturwissenschaften, vol. 27 (6 January 1939), with Fritz Strassmann

fuentes/hahn-strassmann-1939/resumen.texto: Hahn and Strassmann report that barium, a much lighter element, appears among the products of uranium bombarded with neutrons, and they say so with a chemist's caution, because it contradicted the physics of the time. Lise Meitner, who had been part of the team until her exile in 1938, followed the experiments by letter.

fuentes/hahn-strassmann-1939/por_que_imp.texto: It is the chemical proof of nuclear fission; Hahn alone received the 1944 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

fuentes/fision-meitner-frisch/titulo.texto: Disintegration of Uranium by Neutrons: a New Type of Nuclear Reaction

fuentes/fision-meitner-frisch/soporte.texto: Nature, vol. 143 (11 February 1939), with Otto Frisch

fuentes/fision-meitner-frisch/resumen.texto: Meitner and Frisch interpret Hahn's results: the uranium nucleus, unstable like a drop of liquid, splits in two when it absorbs a neutron and releases about 200 million electronvolts, an amount they calculate with Einstein's formula. Frisch called the process “fission”.

fuentes/fision-meitner-frisch/por_que_im.texto: It provided the physical explanation of fission and showed the enormous energy involved.

fuentes/carta-einstein-szilard/soporte.texto: Letter (2 August 1939), delivered by Alexander Sachs on 11 October 1939

fuentes/carta-einstein-szilard/resumen.texto: Drafted by Leó Szilárd and signed by Einstein, the letter warns President Roosevelt that a chain reaction in a large mass of uranium could lead to “extremely powerful bombs of a new type”, and that Germany had stopped the sale of uranium from the Czech mines. It recommends securing a supply of uranium and speeding up research.

fuentes/carta-einstein-szilard/por_que_i.texto: It led to the creation of the Advisory Committee on Uranium, a forerunner of the Manhattan Project; Einstein later said that signing it had been a mistake.

fuentes/memorandum-frisch-peierls/soport.texto: Secret memorandum to the British government (March 1940), with Rudolf Peierls

fuentes/memorandum-frisch-peierls/resume.texto: Frisch and Peierls, refugees at the University of Birmingham, calculate that a few kilograms of pure uranium-235, rather than tons, would be enough for a bomb of devastating effect, and describe how to separate and detonate it. They warn of radioactive fallout and of the possibility that Germany was developing the weapon.

fuentes/memorandum-frisch-peierls/por_qu.texto: It convinced the British government that the bomb was feasible (MAUD Committee) and spurred the American program.

fuentes/informe-franck/soporte.texto: Report to the US Secretary of War (11 June 1945), from the Metallurgical Laboratory in Chicago

fuentes/informe-franck/resumen.texto: Seven Manhattan Project scientists, led by Nobel laureate James Franck and with Leó Szilárd among the signatories, recommend not using the bomb in a surprise attack on Japan and first holding a demonstration before international observers. They warn that an attack without warning would unleash an arms race.

fuentes/informe-franck/por_que_importa.texto: It is the first organized attempt by scientists to influence the use of the nuclear weapon; it did not change the decision.

fuentes/informe-franck/leer.0.titulo.texto: Text of the report (Federation of American Scientists)

fuentes/informe-smyth/soporte.texto: Official US government report (12 August 1945), published as a book by Princeton University Press

fuentes/informe-smyth/resumen.texto: Published days after the bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, the report by physicist Henry Smyth tells the administrative and scientific history of the Manhattan Project: isotope separation, the plutonium production reactors and the organization of Los Alamos, without the details that remained secret.

fuentes/informe-smyth/por_que_importa.texto: It was the official version of the history of the bomb and set what could be said about it in public.

fuentes/atomos-para-la-paz/soporte.texto: Speech to the United Nations General Assembly (8 December 1953)

fuentes/atomos-para-la-paz/resumen.texto: President Eisenhower proposes that the nuclear powers contribute fissionable material to an international agency that would devote it to peaceful uses, such as electricity generation, agriculture and medicine.

fuentes/atomos-para-la-paz/por_que_impor.texto: It led to the creation of the International Atomic Energy Agency (1957) and to the spread of research reactors to many countries, Argentina among them; its critics point out that it also facilitated nuclear proliferation.

fuentes/manifiesto-russell-einstein/auto.texto: Bertrand Russell, Albert Einstein and others

fuentes/manifiesto-russell-einstein/sopo.texto: Statement presented in London on 9 July 1955

fuentes/manifiesto-russell-einstein/resu.texto: Drafted by the philosopher Bertrand Russell and signed by Einstein days before his death, together with nine other scientists, it warns that a war with hydrogen bombs could put an end to the human race and asks governments to renounce war as a means of settling their disputes.

fuentes/manifiesto-russell-einstein/por_.texto: It gave rise to the Pugwash Conferences on Science and World Affairs (1957), which received the 1995 Nobel Peace Prize together with Joseph Rotblat.

fuentes/manifiesto-russell-einstein/leer.texto: Text on the Pugwash Conferences website

fuentes/primer-laser/resumen.texto: Maiman reports that a ruby crystal illuminated with a flash lamp emits a beam of coherent red light of a single wavelength. The journal Physical Review Letters had rejected his first manuscript.

fuentes/primer-laser/por_que_importa.texto: It was the first laser, the basis of optical fibers, disc reading, eye surgery and many industrial processes; the 1964 Nobel Prize in Physics honored the theory of masers and lasers (Charles Townes, Nikolay Basov and Aleksandr Prokhorov).

fuentes/mecanismo-de-higgs/titulo.texto: Broken Symmetries and the Masses of Gauge Bosons

fuentes/mecanismo-de-higgs/resumen.texto: Higgs shows that in certain field theories spontaneous symmetry breaking gives mass to the force-carrying particles, and points out that the mechanism implies a new spin-zero particle. François Englert and Robert Brout, on the one hand, and Gerald Guralnik, Carl Hagen and Tom Kibble, on the other, published equivalent ideas the same year.

fuentes/mecanismo-de-higgs/por_que_impor.texto: It is part of the Standard Model of particle physics; the predicted boson was detected at CERN in 2012, and Higgs and Englert received the 2013 Nobel Prize in Physics.

fuentes/deteccion-del-higgs/titulo.texto: Observation of a New Particle in the Search for the Standard Model Higgs Boson

fuentes/deteccion-del-higgs/soporte.texto: Physics Letters B, vol. 716 (two articles, one by ATLAS and one by CMS)

fuentes/deteccion-del-higgs/resumen.texto: The two large experiments at the Large Hadron Collider, each with its own detector and thousands of authors, report a new particle of about 125 GeV, compatible with the Higgs boson, with a statistical significance of five standard deviations. They had announced it at CERN on 4 July 2012.

fuentes/deteccion-del-higgs/por_que_impo.texto: It completed the experimental verification of the Standard Model of particle physics.

fuentes/ondas-gravitacionales/titulo.texto: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger

fuentes/ondas-gravitacionales/resumen.texto: More than a thousand researchers report that the two LIGO detectors, at Hanford and Livingston, recorded on 14 September 2015 the signal produced by the merger of two black holes of about 36 and 29 solar masses, some 1.3 billion light-years away.

fuentes/ondas-gravitacionales/por_que_im.texto: It was the first direct detection of gravitational waves, predicted by Einstein in 1916, and opened up gravitational-wave astronomy; Rainer Weiss, Kip Thorne and Barry Barish received the 2017 Nobel Prize in Physics.

fuentes/origen-de-las-especies/resumen.texto: Darwin argues that species change over time and descend from common ancestors, and that the main mechanism is natural selection: in the struggle for existence, individuals with favorable variations survive and reproduce more. He gathers evidence from animal breeding, geographical distribution, fossils and embryology.

fuentes/origen-de-las-especies/por_que_i.texto: It founded evolutionary biology; Alfred Russel Wallace had arrived at the same idea, presented together with Darwin's in 1858.

fuentes/teoria-de-maxwell/titulo.texto: A Dynamical Theory of the Electromagnetic Field

fuentes/teoria-de-maxwell/soporte.texto: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London, vol. 155

fuentes/teoria-de-maxwell/resumen.texto: Maxwell brings together the laws of electricity and magnetism in a system of equations, deduces that disturbances of the field propagate as waves at the speed of light and concludes that light is an electromagnetic wave.

fuentes/teoria-de-maxwell/por_que_import.texto: It predicted radio waves, which Heinrich Hertz produced in 1887, and is the basis of electrical engineering and telecommunications.

fuentes/leyes-de-mendel/soporte.texto: Verhandlungen des naturforschenden Vereines in Brünn, vol. 4 (read in 1865)

fuentes/leyes-de-mendel/resumen.texto: With eight years of crosses of peas, Mendel shows that traits are inherited as discrete units that combine in fixed ratios, such as 3 to 1 in the second generation, and formulates the rules of segregation and independent assortment.

fuentes/leyes-de-mendel/por_que_importa.texto: Ignored until 1900, when it was rediscovered by Hugo de Vries, Carl Correns and Erich von Tschermak, it is the basis of genetics.

fuentes/leyes-de-mendel/leer.1.titulo.texto: English translation by William Bateson, “Experiments in plant-hybridisation” (Internet Archive)

fuentes/patente-de-edison/resumen.texto: Edison patents an incandescent lamp with a high-resistance carbon filament inside an evacuated glass bulb. The high resistance made it possible to power many lamps in parallel from a central station.

fuentes/patente-de-edison/por_que_import.texto: The lamp was part of a complete system for generating and distributing electricity, which Edison put into operation in New York in 1882.

fuentes/patente-de-edison/leer.0.titulo.texto: Patent text and images on Google Patents

fuentes/arrhenius-1896/titulo.texto: On the Influence of Carbonic Acid in the Air upon the Temperature of the Ground

fuentes/arrhenius-1896/resumen.texto: Arrhenius calculates by hand how much the Earth's temperature would change if atmospheric carbon dioxide (then called carbonic acid) varied, and estimates that doubling it would raise it by about 5 to 6 °C. He was seeking to explain the ice ages; he later pointed out that burning coal could warm the planet.

fuentes/arrhenius-1896/por_que_importa.texto: It is the first calculation of the greenhouse effect of CO₂, a forerunner of climate change science.

fuentes/tsiolkovski-1903/titulo.texto: The Exploration of Cosmic Space by Means of Reaction Devices

fuentes/tsiolkovski-1903/resumen.texto: Tsiolkovsky derives the equation that relates a rocket's final velocity to the exhaust velocity of the gases and to the ratio between its initial and final mass, and concludes that only a liquid-fuel rocket, using hydrogen and oxygen for example, could reach the speed needed to go into space.

fuentes/tsiolkovski-1903/por_que_importa.texto: It is the theoretical basis of astronautics; the rocket equation bears his name.

fuentes/patente-de-los-wright/resumen.texto: The Wrights patent their system of lateral control by wing warping, combined with a vertical rudder, which allows the pilot to keep balance and turn. The patent, based on their 1902 glider, does not describe the engine.

fuentes/patente-de-los-wright/por_que_im.texto: Three-axis control is the basis of aircraft piloting; defending the patent led to long lawsuits with other builders.

fuentes/patente-de-los-wright/leer.0.tit.texto: Patent text and images on Google Patents

fuentes/goddard-1919/titulo.texto: A Method of Reaching Extreme Altitudes

fuentes/goddard-1919/resumen.texto: Goddard presents his theory and his tests with gunpowder rockets, funded by the Smithsonian Institution, and calculates that a multistage rocket could reach the Moon and mark its arrival with a flash of powder. The press mocked the idea; The New York Times retracted in 1969.

fuentes/goddard-1919/por_que_importa.texto: It was the basis of his work with liquid-fuel rockets, the first of which he launched in 1926.

fuentes/goddard-1919/leer.0.titulo.texto: Smithsonian Miscellaneous Collections 71 (1919), scan from the Smithsonian Libraries

fuentes/insulina-1922/titulo.texto: Pancreatic Extracts in the Treatment of Diabetes Mellitus

fuentes/insulina-1922/soporte.texto: Canadian Medical Association Journal, vol. 12 (March 1922), with Charles Best, James Collip, Walter Campbell and Andrew Fletcher

fuentes/insulina-1922/resumen.texto: It reports the first results in patients of the pancreatic extract prepared in Toronto: in Leonard Thompson, a 14-year-old boy, and in other diabetics, blood and urine sugar fell and their general condition improved. James Collip had purified the extract enough for use in humans.

fuentes/insulina-1922/por_que_importa.texto: It turned type 1 diabetes from a fatal disease into a chronic one; Banting and John Macleod received the 1923 Nobel Prize in Medicine.

fuentes/insulina-1922/leer.0.titulo.texto: Text of the article in the Canadian Medical Association Journal (1922), PubMed Central

fuentes/penicilina-fleming/titulo.texto: On the Antibacterial Action of Cultures of a Penicillium

fuentes/penicilina-fleming/soporte.texto: British Journal of Experimental Pathology, vol. 10

fuentes/penicilina-fleming/resumen.texto: Fleming describes how a mold that contaminated a staphylococcus plate in 1928 dissolved the nearby colonies, and how the filtered culture broth, which he calls “penicillin”, inhibits many bacteria without harming white blood cells. He proposes it mainly for isolating bacteria in the laboratory and suggests a possible use as an antiseptic.

fuentes/penicilina-fleming/por_que_impor.texto: It is the discovery of the first antibiotic; Fleming shared the 1945 Nobel Prize in Medicine with Florey and Chain, who turned it into a medicine.

fuentes/penicilina-fleming/leer.0.titulo.texto: Text of the article in the British Journal of Experimental Pathology (1929), PubMed Central

fuentes/penicilina-oxford/autor.texto: Ernst Chain, Howard Florey and others

fuentes/penicilina-oxford/resumen.texto: The Oxford team, in which Norman Heatley developed the extraction method, reports that purified penicillin protected mice infected with lethal doses of streptococci and other bacteria. In 1941 they tested it on the first patients.

fuentes/penicilina-oxford/por_que_import.texto: It showed that penicillin could cure infections and led to its industrial production in the US during the war.

fuentes/experimento-de-avery/titulo.texto: Studies on the chemical nature of the substance inducing transformation of pneumococcal types

fuentes/experimento-de-avery/autor.texto: Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod and Maclyn McCarty

fuentes/experimento-de-avery/resumen.texto: At the Rockefeller Institute, the authors purify the substance that transforms harmless pneumococci into virulent ones and show that it is deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), not a protein.

fuentes/experimento-de-avery/por_que_imp.texto: It was the first evidence that DNA is the hereditary material.

fuentes/experimento-de-avery/leer.0.titu.texto: Article in the Journal of Experimental Medicine, 1944 (PubMed Central)

fuentes/estructura-del-adn/titulo.texto: Molecular structure of nucleic acids: a structure for deoxyribose nucleic acid

fuentes/estructura-del-adn/soporte.texto: Nature, vol. 171 (25 April 1953), with Francis Crick

fuentes/estructura-del-adn/resumen.texto: In a single page, Watson and Crick propose that DNA consists of two helical chains coiled in opposite directions, joined by base pairs (adenine with thymine, guanine with cytosine). They note that this pairing suggests a copying mechanism for the genetic material. They used X-ray diffraction data from Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins, published in the same issue.

fuentes/estructura-del-adn/por_que_impor.texto: It marks the beginning of molecular biology; Watson, Crick and Wilkins received the 1962 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

fuentes/foto-51/soporte.texto: Nature, vol. 171 (25 April 1953), with Raymond Gosling

fuentes/foto-51/resumen.texto: Franklin and Gosling, of King's College London, present their X-ray diffraction photographs of the B form of DNA, among them “Photo 51” from May 1952, and conclude that their data are consistent with a helix of two or more chains with the phosphates on the outside. Watson had seen that photo in January 1953: Wilkins showed it to him without Franklin's knowledge.

fuentes/foto-51/por_que_importa.texto: It provided the experimental evidence for the double helix; Franklin's role was recognized late.

fuentes/vacuna-de-salk/titulo.texto: Studies in human subjects on active immunization against poliomyelitis

fuentes/vacuna-de-salk/soporte.texto: Journal of the American Medical Association, vol. 151 (28 March 1953)

fuentes/vacuna-de-salk/resumen.texto: Salk reports that his vaccine of formalin-inactivated polioviruses produced antibodies against all three types of the virus in children and adults in Pittsburgh, without serious adverse effects.

fuentes/vacuna-de-salk/por_que_importa.texto: It paved the way for the 1954 field trial, in which 1.8 million children took part, and for the approval of the vaccine in 1955.

fuentes/celula-solar/titulo.texto: A new silicon p-n junction photocell for converting solar radiation into electrical power

fuentes/celula-solar/autor.texto: Daryl Chapin, Calvin Fuller and Gerald Pearson

fuentes/celula-solar/resumen.texto: The three Bell Laboratories researchers describe a silicon cell with a p-n junction that converts about 6% of sunlight into electricity, several times more than selenium cells. They had presented it to the public in April 1954.

fuentes/celula-solar/por_que_importa.texto: It was the first practical solar cell; silicon cells powered satellites from 1958 onward and today dominate solar energy.

fuentes/dogma-central/soporte.texto: Symposia of the Society for Experimental Biology, vol. 12 (1957 lecture)

fuentes/dogma-central/resumen.texto: Crick formulates two hypotheses: the sequence hypothesis, according to which the order of bases in a nucleic acid determines the order of amino acids in a protein, and the “central dogma”, according to which information passes from nucleic acids to proteins and does not flow back. He also anticipates the existence of adaptor molecules, which turned out to be transfer RNAs.

fuentes/dogma-central/por_que_importa.texto: It shaped the research program of molecular biology in the following decades.

fuentes/curva-de-keeling-1960/titulo.texto: The concentration and isotopic abundances of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere

fuentes/curva-de-keeling-1960/resumen.texto: Using precision analyzers installed at Mauna Loa, in Antarctica and at other sites, Keeling shows that atmospheric CO₂ follows an annual cycle driven by Northern Hemisphere vegetation and suggests that its average is rising at a rate comparable to that of fossil fuel burning.

fuentes/curva-de-keeling-1960/por_que_im.texto: It is the first report from the series of continuous measurements that has documented the rise in atmospheric CO₂ since 1958.

fuentes/curva-de-keeling-1960/leer.0.tit.texto: Scripps CO2 Program page with the PDF of the article

fuentes/codigo-genetico/titulo.texto: The dependence of cell-free protein synthesis in E. coli upon naturally occurring or synthetic polyribonucleotides

fuentes/codigo-genetico/soporte.texto: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, vol. 47 (October 1961), with Heinrich Matthaei

fuentes/codigo-genetico/resumen.texto: Nirenberg and Matthaei add a synthetic RNA made only of uracil to a bacterial extract and obtain a protein made only of phenylalanine: the triplet UUU codes for that amino acid. It was the first “codon” to be deciphered; the complete code was established by around 1966.

fuentes/codigo-genetico/por_que_importa.texto: It opened the deciphering of the genetic code; Nirenberg shared the 1968 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Har Gobind Khorana and Robert Holley.

fuentes/discurso-de-la-luna/titulo.texto: Address at Rice University on the Nation's Space Effort

fuentes/discurso-de-la-luna/resumen.texto: Kennedy defends the goal, announced in 1961, of landing a man on the Moon before the end of the decade: “We choose to go to the Moon in this decade and do the other things, not because they are easy, but because they are hard”. He presents the space race as a competition in which the US must not fall behind.

fuentes/discurso-de-la-luna/por_que_impo.texto: It is the best-known public justification of the Apollo program, which reached the Moon in 1969.

fuentes/manabe-wetherald-1967/titulo.texto: Thermal equilibrium of the atmosphere with a given distribution of relative humidity

fuentes/manabe-wetherald-1967/soporte.texto: Journal of the Atmospheric Sciences, vol. 24 (May 1967), with Richard Wetherald

fuentes/manabe-wetherald-1967/resumen.texto: Using a single-column model of the atmosphere that includes convection and water vapor, Manabe and Wetherald calculate that doubling CO₂ would raise surface temperature by about 2 °C and cool the stratosphere.

fuentes/manabe-wetherald-1967/por_que_im.texto: It is considered the first reliable calculation of warming from greenhouse gases; Manabe received the 2021 Nobel Prize in Physics for his climate models.

fuentes/pcr-mullis/titulo.texto: Specific enzymatic amplification of DNA in vitro: the polymerase chain reaction

fuentes/pcr-mullis/soporte.texto: Cold Spring Harbor Symposia on Quantitative Biology, vol. 51, with Fred Faloona and others

fuentes/pcr-mullis/resumen.texto: Mullis and his Cetus colleagues describe the method: the DNA is heated to separate its strands, two primers that flank the target fragment are added, and a polymerase copies it; by repeating the cycle, the amount doubles each time. A first application, to the diagnosis of sickle-cell anemia, had been published in Science in 1985.

fuentes/pcr-mullis/por_que_importa.texto: PCR is a basic technique in molecular biology, forensic science and the diagnosis of infections such as COVID-19; Mullis received the 1993 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

fuentes/aislamiento-del-vih/titulo.texto: Isolation of a T-lymphotropic retrovirus from a patient at risk for AIDS

fuentes/aislamiento-del-vih/soporte.texto: Science, vol. 220 (20 May 1983), with Luc Montagnier and others

fuentes/aislamiento-del-vih/resumen.texto: The Pasteur Institute team describes a new retrovirus, isolated from a patient's lymph node, distinct from the known HTLV viruses. In 1984 Robert Gallo's team in the US confirmed that a virus of this kind causes AIDS; after a dispute over priority, it was named HIV in 1986.

fuentes/aislamiento-del-vih/por_que_impo.texto: It made possible the development of the screening test (1985) and of antiretroviral drugs; Barré-Sinoussi and Montagnier received the 2008 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

fuentes/primer-informe-del-ipcc/titulo.texto: Climate Change: The IPCC Scientific Assessment

fuentes/primer-informe-del-ipcc/autor.texto: Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), Working Group I

fuentes/primer-informe-del-ipcc/soporte.texto: IPCC First Assessment Report (Cambridge University Press, 1990)

fuentes/primer-informe-del-ipcc/resumen.texto: The report concludes that human emissions are substantially increasing the concentrations of greenhouse gases and that this will result in additional warming of the surface; without action, it projects an increase of about 0.3 °C per decade in the 21st century. It notes that the warming observed up to then was consistent with the models, but also with natural variability.

fuentes/primer-informe-del-ipcc/por_que_.texto: It was the scientific basis for the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (1992).

fuentes/primer-informe-del-ipcc/leer.0.t.texto: Full report of Working Group I (IPCC)

fuentes/erradicacion-de-la-viruela-resol.texto: Declaration of global eradication of smallpox
Resolution WHA33.3 of the Thirty-third World Health Assembly (8 May 1980)

The assembly of the World Health Organization declares that the world and all its peoples have won freedom from smallpox, following the intensified program launched in 1967, which combined vaccination with surveillance to stop outbreaks. The last natural case was recorded in Somalia in 1977.
Smallpox is the only human disease to have been eradicated; the surveillance and containment method served as a model for other campaigns.

fuentes/oveja-dolly/titulo.texto: Viable offspring derived from fetal and adult mammalian cells

fuentes/oveja-dolly/soporte.texto: Nature, vol. 385 (27 February 1997), with Keith Campbell and others

fuentes/oveja-dolly/resumen.texto: Wilmut, Keith Campbell and their colleagues transfer the nucleus of mammary gland cells from an adult ewe into enucleated eggs and obtain a lamb, Dolly, born on 5 July 1996, genetically identical to the donor.

fuentes/oveja-dolly/por_que_importa.texto: It showed that a specialized adult cell can be reprogrammed to form a complete organism and opened the debate on human cloning.

fuentes/genoma-humano-ihgsc/titulo.texto: Initial sequencing and analysis of the human genome

fuentes/genoma-humano-ihgsc/resumen.texto: The public consortium, made up of twenty centers in six countries, presents the draft sequence of the human genome, covering about 90% of its euchromatic portion. It estimates between 30,000 and 40,000 genes, far fewer than expected, and makes the data freely available.

fuentes/genoma-humano-ihgsc/por_que_impo.texto: It is the main result of the Human Genome Project and the foundation of medical genomics.

fuentes/genoma-humano-celera/titulo.texto: The sequence of the human genome

fuentes/genoma-humano-celera/resumen.texto: Venter and the team of the company Celera Genomics present their sequence of the human genome, obtained with the whole-genome “shotgun” method and partly based on the consortium's public data. They estimate about 26,000 protein-coding genes.

fuentes/genoma-humano-celera/por_que_imp.texto: The competition with Celera sped up the public project; both announced the draft together at the White House in June 2000.

fuentes/arnm-modificado/titulo.texto: Suppression of RNA recognition by Toll-like receptors: the impact of nucleoside modification

fuentes/arnm-modificado/soporte.texto: Immunity, vol. 23 (August 2005), with Michael Buckstein, Houping Ni and Drew Weissman

fuentes/arnm-modificado/resumen.texto: Karikó and Weissman show that synthetic messenger RNA activates the innate immune system and causes inflammation, but that if some nucleosides are replaced with variants found in natural RNA, such as pseudouridine, this effect almost disappears.

fuentes/arnm-modificado/por_que_importa.texto: It made it possible to use messenger RNA as a drug: it is the basis of the Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna COVID-19 vaccines (2020); 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

fuentes/crispr-2012/titulo.texto: A programmable dual-RNA-guided DNA endonuclease in adaptive bacterial immunity

fuentes/crispr-2012/soporte.texto: Science, vol. 337 (17 August 2012), with Martin Jinek (first author), Emmanuelle Charpentier and others

fuentes/crispr-2012/resumen.texto: The teams of Doudna, in Berkeley, and Charpentier, in Umeå, show that the Cas9 protein of the bacterium Streptococcus pyogenes cuts DNA at the site specified by two small RNAs, and that these can be fused into a single “guide” designed to cut any chosen sequence.

fuentes/crispr-2012/por_que_importa.texto: It opened the way to CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, which became the standard tool for modifying genomes; Doudna and Charpentier received the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. The patent was disputed with the Broad Institute.

fuentes/por-que-el-socialismo/resumen.texto: Article that Einstein wrote for the first issue of the socialist journal Monthly Review, published in New York. It argues that the drive for profit and competition among capitalists produces cycles of boom and crisis, inequality and selfishness, and that private control of the press and the financing of parties by large capital give rise to an “oligarchy of private capital.” It proposes a planned economy, with the means of production in the hands of society. It warns, however, that “a planned economy is not yet socialism,” because it may be accompanied by an all-powerful bureaucracy and the “complete enslavement of the individual,” and it asks how individual rights can be protected.

fuentes/por-que-el-socialismo/por_que_im.texto: It is Einstein’s best-known political text. He wrote it as a scientist rather than as an economist, and published it in the first issue of Monthly Review.

fuentes/por-que-el-socialismo/leer.0.tit.texto: Full text on the Monthly Review website

fuentes/que-es-la-vida-schrodinger/titul.texto: What Is Life? The Physical Aspect of the Living Cell

fuentes/que-es-la-vida-schrodinger/sopor.texto: Book (based on the lectures of February 1943 at the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies)

fuentes/que-es-la-vida-schrodinger/resum.texto: Schrödinger asks how physics and chemistry can explain the events that take place within a living organism, and proposes that hereditary information is held in an “aperiodic solid”, whose configuration of covalent chemical bonds stores it. The lectures, at Trinity College, drew some 400 people, among them the Taoiseach Éamon de Valera and his cabinet.

fuentes/que-es-la-vida-schrodinger/por_q.texto: James Watson and Francis Crick acknowledged that the book inspired their early research and that it presented an early theoretical description of how genetic information would be stored. Hermann J. Muller had already described in 1922 the properties of the hereditary molecule that Schrödinger deduces, and wrote in 1960 that what was correct in the book had already been published.

fuentes/sociedad-de-la-mente/resumen.texto: Minsky builds, step by step, a model of human intelligence from the interaction of simple parts, the “agents”, which do not think by themselves; this “society” produces language, memory, learning, consciousness, the sense of self and free will. He began developing the theory in the early 1970s with Seymour Papert, starting from their work with a robot arm, a camera and children’s blocks.

fuentes/sociedad-de-la-mente/por_que_imp.texto: It is the first complete exposition of his theory. It does not attempt to prove anything about artificial intelligence, nor does it rely on brain structures: it is a set of ideas about how thinking works at the conceptual level, which is why many read it as a book of philosophy.

fuentes/la-doble-helice-watson/soporte.texto: Book (memoir; Atheneum in the United States and Weidenfeld & Nicolson in the United Kingdom)

fuentes/la-doble-helice-watson/resumen.texto: Watson’s first-person account of the discovery of the structure of DNA, written fifteen years later. Harvard University Press gave up publishing it after protests from Crick and Wilkins. It was criticized for presenting science as a race for priority, for showing Watson willing to use others’ data behind their backs, and for its sexist portrait of Rosalind Franklin, who had already died (among others, Anne Sayre in “Rosalind Franklin and DNA”); in the epilogue Watson says that his first impressions of her were often wrong and acknowledges her achievements.

fuentes/la-doble-helice-watson/por_que_i.texto: In 1998 the Modern Library ranked it seventh among the hundred best nonfiction books of the 20th century. That a scientist should narrate his work with such intimacy was unusual, and the dispute over the credit for the discovery remains open.

fuentes/rfc-2460/resumen.texto: Specification of version 6 of the Internet Protocol, which the IETF developed to address the exhaustion of IPv4 addresses. It uses 128-bit addresses, simplifies address configuration and processing in routers, and is not compatible with IPv4, so both need transition mechanisms. It replaced RFC 1883 (December 1995), the first standard for IPv6.

fuentes/rfc-2460/por_que_importa.texto: In 1998 IPv6 had the status of a draft standard; RFC 8200, of July 2017, raised it to Internet Standard.

fuentes/rfc-2460/leer.0.titulo.texto: Text on the RFC publisher’s site

fuentes/gpt-2/titulo.texto: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners

fuentes/gpt-2/resumen.texto: Presents GPT-2, a language model with transformer architecture pretrained on WebText, about 8 million web pages linked from Reddit posts with at least 3 karma. It is a direct scale-up of GPT-1, with ten times the parameters and training data, and without task-specific training it translates, answers questions and summarizes texts. OpenAI released it in stages: a partial version in February 2019 and the full model, with 1.5 billion parameters, on 5 November 2019.

fuentes/gpt-2/por_que_importa.texto: OpenAI initially withheld the code and justified the gradual release by the risk of malicious use; some researchers argued that the threat was exaggerated, and in November 2019 the company itself said it had not seen “strong evidence of misuse”. It was the direct predecessor of GPT-3.

fuentes/gpt-1/titulo.texto: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training

fuentes/gpt-1/resumen.texto: Presents GPT-1, OpenAI's first large language model and the model later known as GPT (generative pre-trained transformer), a name the report does not yet use. It is a decoder-only transformer with twelve layers and 117 million parameters, trained in two stages: unsupervised pre-training on unlabeled text and supervised fine-tuning for each task, with minimal changes to the architecture. It outperformed models designed for each task on several tests: it improved the best previous results by between 1.5 and 5.8% on natural language inference, by 5.7% on the RACE reading comprehension test and by 8.9% on Story Cloze, and it scored 72.8 on GLUE against the previous 68.9.

fuentes/gpt-1/por_que_importa.texto: It is the starting point of the GPT series: it applied to a language model the transformer that Google had introduced in 2017, and it showed that pre-training on unlabeled text was useful for many tasks. GPT-2, from 2019, expanded it.

personas/planck/resumen.texto: German physicist, professor in Berlin. In 1900 he proposed that the energy of radiation is exchanged in quanta, the starting point of quantum physics; he received the 1918 Nobel Prize in Physics.

personas/einstein/resumen.texto: German-born physicist. In 1905, while working as a clerk at the patent office in Bern, he published the papers on light quanta, Brownian motion and special relativity, and in 1915 he formulated general relativity. 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics; he emigrated to the United States in 1933.

personas/marie-curie/resumen.texto: Polish physicist and chemist based in Paris. With Pierre Curie she discovered polonium and radium and coined the term “radioactivity”; she was the first person to win two Nobel Prizes (Physics 1903, Chemistry 1911).

personas/rutherford/resumen.texto: New Zealand physicist. He explained radioactivity as the transmutation of elements (1908 Nobel Prize in Chemistry), proposed in Manchester the nuclear model of the atom (1911) and directed the Cavendish Laboratory from 1919.

personas/bohr/resumen.texto: Danish physicist. His 1913 atomic model applied quanta to the structure of the atom, and the institute he founded in Copenhagen was the center of quantum mechanics. 1922 Nobel Prize in Physics.

personas/heisenberg/resumen.texto: German physicist. He formulated matrix mechanics in 1925 and the uncertainty principle in 1927; 1932 Nobel Prize in Physics. During the Second World War he was the leading figure of the German nuclear program, which did not produce a bomb.

personas/schrodinger/resumen.texto: Austrian physicist. In 1926, in Zurich, he published the wave equation that bears his name, the basis of wave mechanics; he shared the 1933 Nobel Prize in Physics with Paul Dirac.

personas/meitner/resumen.texto: Austrian physicist, for three decades a collaborator of Otto Hahn in Berlin. Exiled in Sweden in 1938, she and her nephew Otto Frisch interpreted Hahn's results as the fission of the uranium nucleus; the 1944 Nobel Prize went to Hahn alone.

personas/otto-hahn/resumen.texto: German chemist. In December 1938, with Fritz Strassmann, he detected barium in uranium bombarded with neutrons, the chemical proof of fission; he alone received the 1944 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

personas/otto-frisch/resumen.texto: Austrian-British physicist. With his aunt Lise Meitner he explained nuclear fission (1939); with Rudolf Peierls he calculated in 1940 that a uranium bomb was feasible, and he later worked at Los Alamos.

personas/fermi/resumen.texto: Italian physicist. He studied neutron-induced reactions in Rome (1938 Nobel Prize in Physics), emigrated to the United States and in 1942 led the first nuclear reactor, Chicago Pile-1, in Chicago.

personas/szilard/resumen.texto: Hungarian-American physicist. He conceived the nuclear chain reaction in 1933, drafted the letter to Roosevelt that Einstein signed in 1939 and worked on the first reactor in Chicago; in 1945 he promoted petitions against using the bomb on cities.

personas/oppenheimer/resumen.texto: American theoretical physicist. He directed the Los Alamos laboratory, where the first atomic bombs were designed. In 1954 the Atomic Energy Commission revoked his security clearance; the Department of Energy vacated that decision in 2022.

personas/hubble/resumen.texto: American astronomer at the Mount Wilson Observatory. In 1924 he showed that there are galaxies beyond the Milky Way, and in 1929 he published the relationship between the distance of galaxies and their recession velocity, evidence of the expansion of the universe.

personas/eddington/resumen.texto: British astrophysicist at Cambridge. He organized the 1919 eclipse expeditions that measured the bending of light predicted by general relativity and popularized the theory in the English-speaking world.

personas/maiman/resumen.texto: American physicist at Hughes Research Laboratories. On 16 May 1960 he operated the first laser, using a ruby crystal.

personas/peter-higgs/resumen.texto: British physicist at the University of Edinburgh. In 1964 he proposed the mechanism that gives particles mass and predicted the boson that bears his name, detected at CERN in 2012; 2013 Nobel Prize in Physics with François Englert.

personas/turing/resumen.texto: British mathematician. In 1936 he defined the Turing machine and the limits of computability; during the war he worked at Bletchley Park on breaking Enigma, and in 1950 he raised the question of whether machines can think. Convicted in 1952 for homosexuality, he died in 1954.

personas/von-neumann/resumen.texto: Hungarian-American mathematician at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton. He founded game theory with Oskar Morgenstern, worked on the Manhattan Project and in 1945 described the stored-program computer architecture that bears his name.

personas/shannon/resumen.texto: American mathematician and engineer. His 1937 thesis applied Boolean algebra to switching circuits and his 1948 paper founded information theory; he worked at Bell Laboratories and at MIT.

personas/vannevar-bush/resumen.texto: American engineer. During the Second World War he headed the Office of Scientific Research and Development, which coordinated radar and the beginnings of the Manhattan Project; in 1945 he envisioned the “memex” and proposed public funding of science.

personas/mauchly/resumen.texto: American physicist. With J. Presper Eckert he designed ENIAC at the Moore School of the University of Pennsylvania, and later UNIVAC, the first commercial computer in the United States.

personas/tommy-flowers/resumen.texto: Engineer at the British Post Office Research Station at Dollis Hill (London). He designed and built Colossus (1943-1944), the electronic valve machine that helped break German communications encrypted with the Lorenz machine.

personas/shockley/resumen.texto: American physicist. He led the Bell Laboratories group that invented the transistor and created the junction transistor; he shared the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics with Bardeen and Brattain. His company in California brought together those who later founded Fairchild; in his later years he advocated eugenicist views.

personas/bardeen/resumen.texto: American physicist. With Walter Brattain he built the first transistor in 1947; he is the only person with two Nobel Prizes in Physics (1956, for the transistor, and 1972, for the theory of superconductivity).

personas/brattain/resumen.texto: American experimental physicist at Bell Laboratories. With John Bardeen he built the point-contact transistor in December 1947; 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics.

personas/kilby/resumen.texto: American engineer at Texas Instruments. In September 1958 he operated the first integrated circuit, on germanium; 2000 Nobel Prize in Physics.

personas/noyce/resumen.texto: American physicist, co-founder of Fairchild Semiconductor (1957) and Intel (1968). In 1959 he patented the monolithic silicon integrated circuit, the design that prevailed in the industry.

personas/gordon-moore/resumen.texto: American chemist, co-founder of Fairchild and Intel. In 1965 he predicted that the number of components per integrated circuit would double at regular intervals, “Moore's law”.

personas/mccarthy/resumen.texto: American computer scientist. He coined the term “artificial intelligence” in the Dartmouth proposal (1955), created the Lisp language (1958-1960) and founded AI laboratories at MIT and Stanford. 1971 Turing Award.
